scene.testo: In ancient Rome, your day started before the sun did. No coffee, no alarm clock, no snooze button. You got up in the cold dark and got dressed by feel.
Within twenty minutes, you had to be standing outside a rich man's house. Why? Because if you weren't there, you didn't eat that day. That's not an exaggeration. That was the system.

For hundreds of years, this was daily life for hundreds of thousands of ordinary Romans. We picture togas, marble and emperors giving speeches. The reality was louder, dirtier and stranger than any movie has shown you.
And here's the part that breaks most people's brains. The Romans did not have hours the way you do. So how did they know when to be anywhere? And what would you have done all day?

descrizione:
What did people in ancient Rome actually do all day? Forget the movies. Daily life in ancient Rome began in the dark, with hungry citizens lining up outside rich men's houses just to eat.

In this cartoon history video, we walk through a real Roman morning: the cramped apartments, the noisy streets, the Roman Forum and the strange way Romans measured time.

If you love Roman history, ancient history and weird history, this is the daily life of the Roman Empire as it really was. Would you have survived a day in ancient Rome?
